**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (docs and process only; no build run)

## One main-ward merge - confirmed for the new rule

The new **Side branch** rule gives exactly ONE merge into `main`, and no other:

- A sub-PR merges into `side/<name>` only. Its base is `side/<name>`, its body starts with `Side branch: side/<name>` and ends with `Refs #N`, never `Fixes #N` (a merge into a side branch closes no issue). Its issue keeps `in-review` until the switch PR of its kind or until its own work is complete on `main`.
- `main` enters the side branch through a sync PR, which also merges INTO `side/<name>` (`git merge`, never rebase), not into `main`.
- Exactly one PR takes `side/<name>` to `main`: the side-to-main PR. The rule authorizes its merge, nothing else: "One PR takes `side/<name>` to `main`. It can come before the switches. It uses `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`... The maintainer's word for that PR says who merges it. For `side/path-kernel` it is the coordinator session... It merges when an independent review is clean on the head, and the batch gate, the heavy `motion` and `app` tests and the example catalog suites are green." The merge-ready skill (step 2, `a PR whose head is a side branch (side/*, the PR to main)`) says the same: it merges only by the session the maintainer's word names, with no `--delete-branch`.
- No text in this PR lets a different PR merge into `main` before the cut. The rule's sub-PRs, sync PRs and gates all stay on the side branch. The switch PRs of each kind are ordinary PRs against `main`; the rule does not authorize them to merge early, and the release-cut law is untouched: "A `feat` or breaking PR merges at the minor/major cut" stands, and this PR changes no code. `main` is merged into the side branch through sync PRs, never the other way round, except for the one side-to-main PR.
- The rule's own wording is consistent with the decision record (`docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`): the record's (a) is the one side-to-main merge (coordinator session, merge commit, no `--delete-branch`, `Refs #N`, green batch gate + heavy `motion` and `app` + example catalog), and (b) to (e) describe the kinds switching one at a time on `main`. The rule does not contradict the record or the skill lines; the skill (`merge-ready`, both changed lines) matches the rule's text word for word on the merge author (the session the maintainer's word names) and the issue comment.

## What looks good

- The stable name of the rule is kept; only the pointer and three bullets changed.
- The pointer fix (`docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` does not exist) points to `RECOMMENDED.md` under `## #4024 - Path kernel K0` and to the new record.
- `RECOMMENDED.md` is deliberately unchanged; the record lists exactly the parts of the K0 record it replaces.
- `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md` was checked and has no wrong line (its side-branch lines agree with the rule); it is not changed, as the body says.
- The four citing lines that name **Side branch** (AGENTS.md lines 161, 374, 388 and the work-issue skill) do not contradict the new text.
- `git grep` for the removed strings (`switch-over`, `4024-path-kernel-design`): no file outside `RECOMMENDED.md` (deliberate) and the new record pins them anymore.
- The decision record records the maintainer's words verbatim ("well then we should preemptive bring it up to main..."), and the issue #4023 plan-change comment matches.

## Results

Docs + process only - no build, no gate, no test run (nothing to build; the body says so and I agree). Trial merge with current `origin/main` (`ec314174e`): clean - `git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main` reports "Already up to date"; the PR head is `f299de3ad`, one commit ahead of `main`, no conflicts. No suites owed; no UI, no post, no toolpath; no snapshot, no process-version, no dependency change. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is untouched (empty diff) and the body has `Process change: yes`.

## Checked against the body

- `Changelog: none` (docs-only, no row needed). `Fixes #4325` at the end. `Process change: yes` present. No `CHANGELOG.md` edit. No `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` edit. `Effort: medium` present.
- The issue #4325 "Done means": the record and the rule agree with the plan of 2026-11-27; `Process change: yes`; no PROCESS_VERSION edit - all met.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `RECOMMENDED.md` still pins the old "switch-over" text. That is the design, not a bug: the record lists the parts it replaces and says the cut does not edit `RECOMMENDED.md` again. Readers must read the record next to the K0 record.
- The decision record says the switch PRs are "its own PR on `main`" and says the Pocket recipe (#3752) is in the side-to-main merge only if it is reviewed by then. The rule text does not repeat the #3752 condition; the rule lists the greenness conditions of the side-to-main PR only. Fine as docs, flagging for the maintainer's awareness.
- `merge-ready`'s retargeted child-base rule (`gh pr edit <child> --base main`) is untouched and consistent with the side-branch rule.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
